gemini_description.purpose: To illustrate the piping layout, water circulation flow path, and installation height constraints of a standard swimming pool filtration system.
gemini_description.summary: This diagram teaches the complete closed-loop filtration cycle of a swimming pool. Water is sucked from the bottom and skimmer outlets of the pool by a self-priming pump, pushed through a multi-port valve into a sand filter tank, and then returned as clean water back to the pool. It highlights a critical installation constraint regarding the maximum suction height of the pump above the pool's water surface.

components.name: Pump
components.description: Labeled in multiple languages (Pump / Pompe / Bomba / Pompa / Pumpe / Bomba / Βόμβα / Насос / قنبلة). It acts as the prime mover that creates suction to draw dirty pool water and pushes it under pressure through the filtration system.

components.name: Pool
components.description: The water reservoir containing a main bottom drain, a side skimmer/overflow outlet, and return inlets on the opposite side to maintain circulation.

components.name: Multi-port Valve
components.description: A selector valve mounted alongside the filter to control the flow direction of water for operations like filtration, backwash, or waste.

components.name: Filter Tank
components.description: A media-filled vessel (typically sand or glass) equipped with an upper diffuser dome and bottom lateral collectors to capture suspended solids from the water.

components.name: Piping and Connectors
components.description: A system of pipes with integrated flow-direction arrows that connect the pool, pump, valve, filter, and drain pit.

procedure: Suction: The pump draws water simultaneously from the pool's bottom main drain and the surface skimmer line.
Delivery to Valve: The pressurized water exits the pump discharge port and enters the inlet of the multi-port valve.
Filtration: The valve directs water to the top of the filter tank where it is dispersed over the sand bed by a diffuser.
Collection: Water flows downward through the sand bed (filtering out debris) and is collected by the lateral assembly at the bottom of the tank.
Return: Filtered water is pushed up the central pipe, exits the filter tank back into the multi-port valve, and is directed through the return line back into the pool inlets.

technical_details.detail: The diagram shows a suction-lift configuration where the pump is installed above the pool's water level.
Flow direction is clearly marked on all pipe segments by small black arrows, defining the loop during normal filtration mode.
An auxiliary waste line connects the multi-port valve to an open-discharge drain pit located below the equipment level.

warnings.warning: The maximum allowable vertical distance between the pool's water level and the pump intake centerline is 2 meters ('Max. 2 m') to prevent priming issues or excessive suction head loss.
